statement.p: (a) Graph r=1/(4\cos\theta) for -\pi/2\le\theta\le\pi/2 and r=1. Then write an iterated integral in polar coordinates representing the area inside the curve r=1 and to the right of r=1/(4\cos\theta). (Use t for \theta in your work.)
(b) Evaluate your integral to find the area.

static.solution:
(a) The curve r=1/(4\cos\theta), or r\cos\theta=1/4, is the line x = 1/4. The curve r=1 is the circle of radius 1 centered at the origin. This gives the graph
The line intersects the circle where 4\cos\theta=1, so \theta = \pm\arccos(1/4). Thus \hbox{Area }=\int_{-\arccos(1/4)}^{\arccos(1/4)}\int_{1/(4\cos\theta)}^1 r\,dr\,d\theta. Evaluating gives \hbox{Area }= \int_{-\arccos(1/4)}^{\arccos(1/4)}\left(\frac{r^2}{2}\bigg|_{1/(4\cos\theta)}^1\right)d\theta =\frac{1}{2}\int_{-\arccos(1/4)}^{\arccos(1/4)}\left(1-\frac{1}{16\cos^2\theta}\right)d\theta so \mbox{Area }=\frac{1}{2}\left(\theta -\frac{\tan\theta}{16}\right) \bigg|_{-\arccos(1/4)}^{\arccos(1/4)} =\frac{1}{2}\left(2(\arccos(1/4)) - 2\frac{\tan(\arccos(1/4))}{16}\right) = \arccos(\frac1{4}) - \frac1{16}\,\tan(\arccos(\frac1{4})).
